sentences: The Voronoi diagram of lines in three dimensions partitions space according to which input line is nearest.
The problem asks for its worst-case combinatorial size under Euclidean distance, with line segments as a related version.
The source conjectures growth close to quadratic in the number of objects.
A bound for one distance level, such as a union of equal-radius cylinders, does not control the entire diagram automatically.
Resolving the complexity would sharpen a basic proximity structure for extended objects in space.
